response.markdown_report:
The strongest initial direction is a **receptive-field-aware recency diagnostic** for the supplied NextItNet. At 0% progress, establishing whether measured temporal failures support an intervention is more defensible than adding architectural complexity.

### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections over broad similarity. This motivates testing recent-history dependence, without treating inferred purpose as observed intent. (2) Existing probes measure embedding geometry and sampled margins. Neither establishes whether temporal information improves recommendations. (3) Left padding and causal convolution determine which history positions can affect predictions. Incorrect readout or padding behavior could invalidate subsequent interpretation.

**Related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) expands historical coverage through dilated causal convolutions. Its receptive field supplies explicit boundaries for diagnostic interventions. (2) The [perturbation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165) reports greater damage from removing recent training interactions. Frozen-model perturbations remain a separate hypothesis requiring measurement. (3) [Evaluation research](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) documents distortions from sampled evaluation. Training margins should therefore accompany target ranks, while the prescribed host metric remains authoritative.

### Framework and candidate directions

| Direction | Evidence | Gap addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation validity | Causality, receptive field, padding | Distinguish implementation faults from model limitations |
| Useful temporal dependence | Controlled history interventions and target ranks | Distinguish sensitivity from predictive benefit |
| Learning intervention | Measured temporal failures and host validation | Test whether diagnosis supports improvement |

Scores below are originality / future potential / code difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

1. **Paired recency probes — 5/8/3.** Originality: useful family-specific synthesis, but established perturbation methods. Potential: creates actionable evidence, but cannot establish current intent. Difficulty: requires no retraining, but careful intervention matching is necessary. References: NextItNet; perturbation study.
2. **Recency-weighted next-item loss — 3/6/2.** Originality: direct diagnostic response, but familiar weighting. Potential: may prioritize recent transitions, but can discard useful older patterns. Difficulty: small loss change, but weighting needs validation. Reference: perturbation study motivates testing, not guaranteed improvement.
3. **Learned gates on dilated residual blocks — 4/7/5.** Originality: integrates scale selection within NextItNet, but gating is established. Potential: permits adaptive historical coverage, but may overfit sparse histories. Difficulty: modest architecture change, but requires predictor and probe updates. Reference: NextItNet.

### Selected algorithm: paired recency probes

Freeze each category’s single trained model. Construct diagnostic targets from training-only prefixes; match recent and older interventions within the actual receptive field by removal count and item-frequency strata. Report unmatched coverage. Repack histories consistently and compare against equally severe control interventions.

```text
verify causality, padding behavior, and final-nonpadding readout
for each eligible training prefix and its next-item target:
    score original, recent-deletion, and older-deletion histories
    record target-rank change and positive–negative margin change
bootstrap users within categories; compute equal-weight macro effects
```

Treat results as diagnostic evidence, not validation gains. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt`; return measured metrics, definitions, sample counts, and unavailable values explicitly. Retain all ModelView hooks. Any subsequent training change keeps the supplied seeds, limits, routing, single-model constraint, and matching predictor writer; selection uses unchanged host validation HR@10.

idea.description: Add paired, receptive-field-aware history interventions to the family-specific NextItNet diagnostic adapter. Compare the predictive effects of removing recent versus older interactions using training-only prefix targets.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests insufficient attention to recent specific interests, while existing embedding and sampled-margin probes cannot determine whether useful temporal dependence is present. Controlled interventions provide a measurable first step without asserting unobserved intent, ownership, compatibility, or personality.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied NextItNet backbone and one checkpoint per category. Compute receptive field from every actual convolution; verify causality and explicitly locate the final nonpadding position in left-padded inputs. Use training-only diagnostic prefixes without changing training or validation splits. Match intervention severity and frequency strata, report matching coverage, and treat insufficient samples as unavailable rather than zero. Full-catalog diagnostic ranking must retain the target and exclude other previously observed items consistently. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView interfaces. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including uncertainty and sample counts. Do not use unavailable review or category metadata. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Host macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion. No model or predictor change is required for the initial diagnostic experiment.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category's frozen trained NextItNet:
  Verify earlier features are invariant to future-token changes.
  Verify effects of padding and interventions outside the actual receptive field.
  Build eligible (training-history prefix, next training item) diagnostic examples.
  For each example:
    Identify matched recent and older deletion sets inside the receptive field.
    Skip unmatched examples and count them.
    Repack and left-pad both perturbed histories identically.
    Extract features through log2feats and gather the final nonpadding index.
    Use predict_score to score the same eligible items for all variants.
    Record original and perturbed target ranks, diagnostic HR@10, and sampled margins.
  Bootstrap users, retaining all prefixes for each sampled user.
Aggregate category effects with equal weights.
Return measured metrics, definitions, uncertainty intervals, and coverage.
Generate an interpretation prompt that separates observations from hypotheses.

originality.positive: Combines NextItNet receptive-field constraints, paired temporal interventions, and rank-based corroboration into a task-specific diagnostic.
originality.negative: Perturbation diagnostics and recency comparisons are established techniques; the contribution is their disciplined integration.

future_potential.positive: Can guide minimal training interventions and make diagnostic claims auditable across all four categories.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic history interventions can shift the input distribution and cannot identify current intent or guarantee validation improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the frozen model and existing feature and scoring hooks without additional fitted predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct matching, eligibility masks, padding handling, and user-level uncertainty estimation require care.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for next-item recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for receptive-field and causality checks.
limitations: Does not establish that temporal perturbation sensitivity identifies user intent or predicts improvement on this benchmark.

related_work.title: Interaction-position perturbation study
contributions: The supplied research summary reports stronger effects from removing recent training interactions.
limitations: Training-data removal evidence does not directly validate inference-time interventions on a frozen NextItNet.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp: recommender evaluation flaws
contributions: Documents evaluation problems involving negative sampling.
Supports corroborating sampled margins with broader ranking diagnostics.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed probes or justify changing the pinned host evaluator.
